court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court, Nagpur, Hindu Marriage Petition No. 1021 of 2013
case_name: Chhandupriya @ Priyanka W/O. Rahul ... vs Rahul S/O. Arun Mohod
facts_of_case: The parties got married in 2013. The respondent-husband filed a petition for nullity of marriage under Section 12(1)(c) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The trial court allowed the petition.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking to set aside a marriage as null and void to prove that the marriage was not consummated.
legal_principles.held: On an appreciation of the material on record, the Family Court allowed the petition filed by the respondent-husband and declared that the marriage is null and void under Section 12(1)(c) of the Hindu Marriage Act.

legal_principles.principle: The court cannot rely on unproven or unreliable evidence to set aside a marriage as null and void.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted that the Family Court erroneously relied on the Urdu writing in the diary at Exhibit 44 though the respondent-husband had not examined the translator.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is admitted and heard finally with the consent of the parties. The marriage is declared null and void.

keywords: Latin maxim: Actus me invito non estactus
